en: Well, so what? You still like them, right? It doesn't matter who bought them.
I suppose. I don't use things I receive if they aren't suited to my tastes.
We talking presents from customers? It must be nice to get lots of gifts.
No, not that. I don't like using things I get from people I hardly know.
That's harsh. I think the most I ever got was a rice ball before a game once.
The purse I typically carry is one my mother used to use, so it's not like someone bought it for me.
It's a hand-me-down?
Yes. My mother also got it from her mother.
So it's an heirloom. Does that mean if you ever have a kid you'll give it to her?
Yes, I certainly hope so!
I take good care of my own equipment, too. Maybe I should let my own kid use it, if I have one.
Oh, how wonderful! You simply must!
It'd be way cheaper, too.
I could get you something new. Regardless of brand, you need something modern for your look.
Goodness no. I don't want to look like some floozy who gets all caught up in trends.
Oh, really? What would you want then?
Perhaps something that shows I know my stuff? Something that people can see right away is stylish.
I see. I guess people with good taste pay attention to that level of detail.
You don't buy stuff for yourself?
No. When I go out with my mother, she buys me the things I want. I hardly ever buy anything on my own.
Wow, you go shopping with your mom? That's real girly of you. I'd be pretty embarrassed to do something like that.
Oh, you should go shopping with your mother, Shinada-san! I'm certain you'd have fun!
Yeah, I think I'll pass on that.
Something bothering you again?
No, it's nothing like that. I have something weighing me down, is all.
Weighing you down?
Earlier today, I went to a wedding for a friend I've known since kindergarten.
She beat you to the punch? Let me guess, she got married before you so you can't be happy for her?
Of course not! Honestly, could you please not interrupt me?
Yikes, guess I was way off base.
It ran long, so I had to come straight from the reception to the club. The wedding party gift was really heavy.
The gift was heavy? What do you mean?
It's in the locker room right now, but it won't actually fit in my locker. How am I supposed to take it home with me?
That's incredible! It's got to be something really valuable, right? You should open it!
I think it might be a pot?
A pot!?
They like to show off, so I should have assumed they would pick out something big.
How Nagoya of them. You people always go big on everything.
Not as many households do that sort of thing anymore, but my friend's family certainly does things the old way.
That's not so bad. I mean it's a wedding, after all. It's a one time thing, so why not go all out like that?
Hehe. You're a good fit for Nagoyan culture, Shinada-san. I'd never have guessed!
Nah, I live too frugally for that. But I'm still a sucker for luxurious things!
Why not complain? Ask for something more practical.
Oh goodness, I could never do something so disrespectful! Who knows what rumors would spread about me?
Well, I don't think talking smack about you behind your back is a very high-class thing to do, either...
What do other families do?
The popular thing to do is to hand out gift catalogs and have guests order what they'd like afterwards.
Neat! No worrying about getting something you already have!
And even if I wanted the same pot, that method would save me the trouble of having to carry a heavy gift around.
Whoever thought of that is a genius!
Yeah, that's a pain. I suppose you'll have to take a cab home?
I suppose. But I already have pots back at home. It's just going to get piled up with the others.
What a dick move. Didn't they consider that people would need to drag these things home?
Exactly! It's Nagoya tradition, though.
Oh? What do you mean?
Being able to provide an extravagant gift shows a family's worth.
I see. So it's about the family not looking like a bunch of cheapskates.
Not only that, but the gifts are paraded out in front of the neighbors when they are moved out of the bride's house.
If it were me, I think I'd be too embarrassed to make myself go through with it.
Yeah. Who's the wedding even for, am I right?
What the hell!? That's just all for the family's sake! They should give out something that's meaningful for the attendees.
Yes, I quite agree. I hope to be able to give my guests something more ideal when it's my turn.
Your wedding gift, huh? I'd be happy to get one, but I'd be a little conflicted about it.
I'll take it! I could use one!
Oh no, it would be rude to pass off a gift I received before I've even gotten it home.
So let me give you a lift home first, and then I can take it off your hands. What do you say?
Well, well! Do you want the pot that badly? I suppose I wouldn't be opposed.
Shinada-san, did you know there are lots of dogs in France?
I did. Isn't it typical over there to own them as pets?
Yes. They have many cats as well, but most households own dogs.
My mother has owned dogs since she was a child, even after coming to Japan.
What kind of dog does she have?
A male French Bulldog. We keep him in the house, so he's always with the family.
Must be noisy. There was a house with a dog near me when I was a kid, and it'd wake me up every morning with its yapping. I hated that thing.
We've trained Ulysses to not bark unless it's necessary. Please don't lump him in with nuisances like that.
My bad.
Why not get a dog of your own, Shinada-san? I'm sure you'll change your opinion of them.
That might be nice. Dogs are smart, and I'd have someone I could play catch with.
Oh, that's a nice idea! Playing with a pet will make sure you get your exercise, so you should definitely do that!
Yeah, I mostly just do practice swings and lift weights. I should give this some more thought.
No way. Pets are expensive. I could never afford one.
I suppose that's true, yes. I bet it would cost more to feed the dog than it would to feed yourself, Shinada-san.
Sadly, I don't think that's far from the truth.
What do you consider necessary? Are there instances where you'd want a dog to bark?
But of course! Why, the other day we had a burglar try to break in during the middle of the night.
No way! Are you serious?
But Ulysses noticed him and started barking, so he ran off without stealing anything. If Ulysses hadn't been there, it would have been awful!
Smart dog. I guess he recognizes people by their faces.
Yes. So he doesn't bark much, and the neighbors haven't complained about him even once.
A dog suits a classy lady like you, Shion-chan. I don't think I'd be as good a fit for one.
I don't need that. A burglar wouldn't find anything worth stealing at my place.
But wouldn't you be in danger if a stranger invaded your home? A guard dog would offer you quite a bit of peace of mind.
Nah, I had a prowler break in once before. I had so little that the guy actually left money FOR me and got the heck out of there.
If I'd had a dog, he would've chased the guy off before that happened.
Oh dear! What kind of place do you live in? I would like to see it sometime!
Really? The only people who come by are debt collectors, so I'd gladly welcome a real guest!
You don't have an alarm?
I... No, we don't.
Why not? If your house is a target for burglars, you should definitely have one installed.
Well, it's complicated. Would you mind dropping the subject?
Oh, sorry. I guess you really do count on that dog of yours.
You don't let him outside?
Oh no, I take him out with me every day.
Ah, so you do make sure to walk him.
It's not really a walk, per se. I don't put him on a leash. I carry him around in my arms.
Wow, you just do as you please, huh? I didn't think pets were meant for carrying around.
That's how it's done in France. People bring them onboard the passenger cabin of planes too.
There are even explicit signs for places where dogs aren't allowed, since having them is so common.
Talk about culture shock. You can't bring your pets into many places here in Japan.
That's rude. I get that it's the Western way of doing things, but what's good for you might be a nuisance to others, don't you think?
Oh, you're the one that's rude! Our dear Ulysses would never be so ill-mannered!
Besides, families in France train their dogs quite rigidly. I'd wager they're far more well-behaved than the dogs here in Japan.
Wow, that's quite a commitment to discipline! Are French owners subjected to that kind of training too?
Did you work today, Shinada-san?
Nah, there was a lot of other stuff going on.
Do you... not know what I do for a living, Shion-chan?
I don't, no.
Oh, good. Er, I mean, I usually work around here, so I'm recognized by a lot of people.
Oh, really? Then I apologize for not having noticed before.
Hehe, no, it's fine! That makes it easier for me, actually.
So, what do you do for a living?
I'm a nightlife journalist. I write articles for both print magazines and online.
Nightlife? So you go to those sorts of establishments and partake of their services?
Yeah! I write articles based on the experience provided to me by the girls.
That's really what you do for work? I had no idea. Would you be able to tell me anything more about it?
Hahaha, you're sure interested in weird things, Shion-chan. Let's save that discussion for another time.
You won't tell me? That's too bad. I'm really curious about you, Shinada-san.
Heheh, it's just tough to say it to a woman.
By the way, where are you from, Shion-chan?
I'm from Nagoya.
So you're from around here. But you don't have much of an accent.
I wouldn't have guessed. You don't have an accent, so I assumed you were from somewhere else.
I try not to speak the Nagoya dialect. I don't like it very much.
I guess it does sound sort of rough.
Yes, that's why I make it a point to speak it as little as possible.
You've had a good upbringing. You're a real Nagoya lady. And quite refined at that!
Oh dear, you can tell? I was trying to keep it a secret.
You're stellar! A real cut above other girls. You just exude good breeding. Clearly, you're the shining star of this club.
Please, don't compare me to the other girls. I'm only concerned about myself.
Oh, sure, all right! Sorry. I wasn't thinking straight there.
You don't have to hide it. I feel like I'm at a high-class club around you.
You're very honest, Shinada-san.
Because I'm a bad liar. People see through me so easily. I trip myself up all the time.
What about me? Do I look like a rich guy?
Hehe. I can't say that you do, no.
See? I wish I could be a high-roller.
Don't worry about it so much. People from Nagoya speak with a certain warmth I like.
Really? It doesn't sound harsh to you, like everyone is always angry?
Maybe sometimes. When I first came to town, my teammates all scared the crap out of me.
But I realized that was because they were all physically buffed, so their way of speaking just intimidated me even more.
It does make one seem less refined, doesn't it? This is why I need to make sure I don't speak Nagoya dialect with other people.
Wait, no, I only meant that for guys. I didn't mean you, Shion-chan!
Not at all. Even if it does sound harsh at times, I know they're not mad at me. They're just really passionate about what they're saying, is all.
They wear their heart on their sleeve, so I like them better than people from Tokyo. When I'm there, sometimes I can't figure out what they're thinking.
I much prefer being forthright than hiding my intentions behind a veil of politeness.
See? That's what I like about Nagoya. So I think it's fine if you relax and speak Nagoya dialect around me, Shion-chan.
Oh. Still, I'm rather shy about it.
Hehe, you're cute when you blush!
Hehe. I feel so much more at ease when you're here, Shinada-san.
You do? How come?
Customers like you are rare, so there are lots of things I'd like to ask you about.
What sorts of things?
Well, for starters, what brings you to Nagoya, Shinada-san?
How am I rare?
Most of the people who work around here are all from here, too. Since you're not from Nagoya, that makes you a more exceptional case.
I see. Well, there are many reasons why I'm here.
Would you mind telling me about yourself? I'm really quite curious!
Well, it's been fifteen years, but I first came here from Tokyo because of work.
